column1: # Apprentice handbook pages (p1 to p7) and diagram annotations.

column2:
1. Double-click Apprentice Intercom, contact agency, and hire an apprentice.
2. In Routines, create a routine (an ordered set of tasks); example routines can be used directly without configuration.
3. Return to Apprentices tab and assign routines. You can assign multiple routines (morning or night shift) in Details. New apprentices work by default; toggle Rest if paused.
4. Morning shift works upon waking before opening; night shift works when you sleep.

Daily workload for an apprentice. Refills upon sleeping after wages are paid; used first for that night's shift, remaining AP carries over to next morning. Actions consume AP; higher proficiency reduces cost. When AP is depleted, remaining work is deferred to next shift starting from task 1.

An apprentice can run multiple routines, executed sequentially in order and sharing daily AP. When multiple apprentices run the same routine, they execute in order from the Apprentices tab, with later apprentices handling remaining items.
Wages are settled every night upon sleeping. If funds are insufficient, apprentices later in the list strike first; unassigned apprentices strike earliest!
Each level adds {0} daily AP, {1} daily wage, and raises proficiency floor by 4 (level 1 is 54), preventing new routines from running too slowly. Studying training materials grants XP.

Apprentices have distinct proficiency (0-100) per routine, viewable in Details. Higher proficiency reduces AP cost: at 100 it is 0.75x base cost, while newcomers start around 1.4x. With default settings, running the same routine continuously reaches 85+ in about two weeks.

Proficiency depends on similarity between past work and current routine. Switching to routines with similar actions and items retains most proficiency; switching to very different ones starts lower. Running multiple disparate routines results in lower proficiency than specializing.
Proficiency only affects AP consumption, not daily wage; wage depends strictly on level!
Common presets (alive, dead, has slot, etc.) can be added directly; numerical values like charge or volume can be specified via Condition.
Pick: All, First N (e.g. lowest charge first 1 item), Exclude First N (e.g. youngest exclude first 2), or aggregate as number (count, sum, etc.).
Selects items to process by specifying scope, item type, conditions, and pick method. Can be created directly within tasks. Can be promoted to global filter for use across routines.
Named numerical values, e.g. "Battery Swap Threshold 30". Can be shared across conditions and adjusted directly in Routines.

Whole shop, specific label, or another filter; multiple can be added. "Contents" refers to contained items; "Itself" refers to container/machine itself (e.g. [Hydroponics] itself with condition "has slot" selects idle hydroponics).

Filters search the whole shop by default (items you own, excluding items for sale). To target specific bays, machines, or containers, name them using the Blue Labeler (e.g. "Hydro Storage") or via "＋ Name..." in the routine editor. Multiple objects can share the same name.
You can directly select custom names ([Name]) as filter target without creating a filter!
Game Tags use the game's own names; a tag an item does not have counts as 0, so a seed without a trait has it at rank 0.

Two extractors take Purifying from Hydroreed Seeds and Nutrient-Poor from Fillerweed Seeds; written disks go to [Gene Bank], and extraction stops once enough are in stock. Using a Precision Extraction Module on a written disk locks it to that trait.
Writes Purifying into the seed in the target slot of [Trait Writer] until the target rank or the heat cap. A seed without a trait counts as rank 0.

Heat only resets through breeding: after writing, the seed goes to [Breeding Hydroponics], and the harvested offspring returns to the writer with 0 heat. Each rank of Nutrient-Poor lowers complexity by 2, offsetting the +3 per rank of Purifying.
Success chance = 95 − 5 × (complexity + heat) + machine quality bonus, at least 5%. Every write or extraction raises the heat, success or not.
Moves items to a container, storage bay, or machine (e.g. move uncharged batteries to recharger). Destination must be a container. You can also choose a slot or a storage tab.

Runs every shift by default. Options like "...when [A] not empty" or "...when [A] less than N" can be chosen; skipped tasks consume no AP. More complex conditions are configured under "Advanced...", e.g. "[A] Water > 1000 ml".
Presses buttons on machine interfaces (start, print, transfer all), unwraps packages, or toggles switches without opening windows.
Pairs two groups of items in order and swaps their positions. If counts differ, excess items remain in place.
Applies a tool to an object, e.g. knife on rat, water jug on empty bottle. Direction is decided by game: faucet on empty bucket fills the bucket.
Which items, in what order, and how many are all defined in filters; the action only decides what to do!
A sub-filter narrows its parent's results and keeps their order unless it has its own sort.

① Swap Low Battery (charge ascending) with Full Battery (charge descending): replaces lowest battery with fullest, leaving depleted battery in recharger.\n② Put uncharged batteries from storage into rechargers with free slots.

Each shift executes in order from Apprentices tab: each apprentice runs their routines sequentially, and tasks run top-to-bottom. Tasks re-evaluate current shop state so already-processed items are not repeated. Adjust order using ↑↓.
Swaps low batteries with full ones, and places uncharged idle batteries into rechargers. Ready to use without configuration.
Harvests crops, replants seeds, swaps water (similar to battery loop), and inserts nutrient tablets.
Moves loose medicine and food into [Medicine Storage] and [Food Storage]; multiple bays can share the same name.
Inserts chips, replenishes filament/materials, and collects finished products.
Refills tanks with clean water, feeds hungry fish, removes dead fish, keeps one adult male and female for breeding, and butchers the rest.
Enables auto-mix on dispenser, replenishes feed, retains breeding stock (1 male, 2 females), slaughters adult rats, and cleans droppings.
Prints water bottles, collects water, purifies to base water, stocks shelves, and collects sales revenue.
Example routines require no configuration. To store outputs in specific bays, name them as used in examples (e.g. "Hydro Storage")!

After the morning shift, an Apprentice Daily Report is issued (on the counter, or in the trash can if the game option is set); double-click to read; the paper summarizes last night's shift and this morning's shift. The Reports tab displays past shifts and daily wages.
